articles.title: Power Outage in Newhey Linked to 'Third-Party Interference'
articles.excerpt: Residents in Newhey experienced a power outage lasting approximately three hours following a loud bang linked to third-party interference on the electricity network.
articles.content_html:
Residents in Newhey, Rochdale, were left without power for around three hours following a loud bang associated with an incident on the electricity network. The disruption occurred on the evening of October 18, 2026, and was reported by Electricity North West, who stated that the outage was due to 'third-party interference' on their high-voltage network.

According to a message from Electricity North West, the loud bang was heard at a property on Ogden Lane at the same time the power interruption occurred. While most residents had their power restored by 23:17, one customer remained without supply as further investigations were conducted to ensure safety before restoration could take place.

Electricity North West expressed appreciation for the patience and understanding of the affected residents during the investigation. They confirmed that their teams were working to identify the root cause of the fault and ensure the safety of the network before restoring power to the remaining customer.

Residents are encouraged to stay updated through official channels for any further developments regarding the power supply in their area. For those affected, it is recommended to check the Electricity North West website or contact their customer service for assistance.

articles.title: Newhey Quarry’s 250-home allocation needs a clearer account of remediation and affordability
articles.excerpt: Newhey Quarry is allocated for around 250 homes, with additional parking intended to support the nearby tram stop. The council’s land assessment classifies the site as brownfield, but the quarry’s history makes its treatment more complicated than simply describing it as unused land.
articles.content_html:
Newhey Quarry is allocated for around 250 homes, with additional parking intended to support the nearby tram stop. The council’s land assessment classifies the site as brownfield, but the quarry’s history makes its treatment more complicated than simply describing it as unused land.

The allocation topic paper records mineral-working consent extending to 2042 and earlier objections that the proposed housing might not match local affordability needs. Those historic records do not establish current extraction activity or a final permission to build homes.

Restoration obligations, ground stability and the definition of previously developed land need to be checked in the actual application. The existence of a quarry alone is insufficient to settle all those issues.

No verified builder, price list or affordable tenure schedule was established in this review. Residents therefore cannot yet be told how many homes will be socially rented or accessible to first-time buyers.

Tram access is a benefit, but it does not establish capacity in schools, GP services, sewers or the local road network. A phased remediation and infrastructure programme will be needed to show that the allocation can become a safe neighbourhood.

The potential 250 homes contribute to the long-term pipeline. They should not be counted as completed housing, nor allocated to an unverified developer’s legal record.

Location: Huddersfield Road, Newhey

Planning stage: Strategic allocation; current detailed permission and builder not established

Homes: Around 250 allocation homes

Let or for sale: Affordable housing envisaged; numbers, tenure, rents and sale prices unknown

Land: Council assessment identifies brownfield; historic Green Belt and mineral-restoration context require care

Final planning agreement: Allocation-stage evidence: no current detailed permission, executed deed or final housebuilder established.

Exact rents / prices: No exact future rent, sale price, service charge or estate-charge schedule was established from the council/government material reviewed; no reliable scheme-specific current quotation was identified.

Affordable breakdown: No secured affordable count or tenure split established.

Funded school capacity: No scheme-specific funded additional school places, named capital project and opening date were established from the accessible official records reviewed.

Funded healthcare capacity: No site-specific funded NHS expansion, additional staffed appointment capacity or delivery date was established from the accessible council/government records reviewed. Proximity to a surgery is not a capacity assessment.

Funded transport capacity: Extra tram-stop parking is envisaged. No funded delivery contract, additional tram-service capacity or complete highways package verified.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.

Read the borough-wide housing investigation and the other developments: https://rochdaledaily.co.uk/articles/rochdale-housing-developments-affordability-schools-gp-transport.html

articles.title: PW Greenhalgh Finishing Limited Entering Creditors' Voluntary Liquidation
articles.excerpt: PW Greenhalgh Finishing Limited, based in Newhey, Rochdale, is undergoing a creditors' voluntary liquidation following a resolution passed by its directors.
articles.content_html:
PW Greenhalgh Finishing Limited, located at Ogden Mill, Ogden Lane, Newhey, Rochdale, OL16 3TQ, has entered into a creditors' voluntary liquidation. This decision follows a resolution passed by the company's directors, as detailed in an official notice published in The Gazette.

The joint liquidators appointed to oversee the process are Jason Mark Elliott and Craig Johns, both from Cowgills Limited, whose office is situated at Fourth Floor, Unit 5B, The Parklands, Bolton, BL6 4SD. They will manage the liquidation process in accordance with the Insolvency Act 1986.

For those seeking further information regarding the liquidation, Aniser Hussain can be contacted at Cowgills Limited via telephone at 0161 827 1200 or by email at aniser.hussain@cowgills.co.uk.

This development may impact employees and creditors of PW Greenhalgh Finishing Limited, as the liquidation process will involve settling outstanding debts and determining the future of the company's assets.

articles.title: Newhey Gardening Gang volunteers transform churchyard in latest community clean-up
articles.excerpt: Volunteers from Newhey's Gardening Gang have completed another major session in the local churchyard, cutting grass, tending shrub beds and cremation plots and clearing pathways.
articles.content_html:
A team of community volunteers has continued its work keeping a Newhey churchyard looking its best after another strong turnout for the local Gardening Gang.

Volunteers were back at work yesterday, tackling a substantial list of jobs across the churchyard and continuing the improvements made during previous sessions.

The group's 'buzzy bee strimmers' were out in force and completed the mammoth task of cutting all of the grass areas. Other volunteers weeded and cut back shrub beds and cremation plots, while a number of pathways were also cleared.

The work is part of an ongoing community effort to maintain and improve the churchyard, with local volunteers giving their own time to care for a space used by families, visitors and the wider Newhey community.

Organisers thanked everyone who took part, saying the churchyard continues to look great thanks to the efforts of the Gardening Gang.

Volunteer-led projects like this can make a significant difference to shared spaces, particularly where regular maintenance involves large areas of grass, established planting and paths which need repeated attention throughout the growing season.

The Gardening Gang is expected to announce another volunteering date, with residents being encouraged to watch for details of the next session.

Rochdale Daily would like to thank all of the volunteers giving their time to help look after Newhey's community spaces.
articles.right_to_reply: Community groups in Newhey can send volunteering dates, photographs and local updates to news@rochdaledaily.co.uk.

articles.title: Elderly lady found after incredible community effort
articles.excerpt: A woman in her 70s who went missing in Newhey has been found after hundreds of residents joined Greater Manchester Police in an extraordinary community search.
articles.content_html:
An elderly woman who went missing in Newhey has been found following an extraordinary community effort involving hundreds of local residents.

Christine, who is in her 70s, was reported missing earlier in the evening, prompting an urgent response from Greater Manchester Police and a huge mobilisation across Newhey and the surrounding area.

As concern grew, residents left their homes to help officers search on the ground. People walked streets, paths and open spaces, checked nearby areas and shared information rapidly across community groups in an effort to bring Christine home.

The response was remarkable. Hundreds of people are understood to have assisted either directly with searches or by sharing appeals and helping coordinate information alongside GMP.

At around 11pm, local woman Charlotte Rigby found Christine. In a touching detail after hours of worry, Christine was found clutching a bunch of flowers.

News that she had been located was met with enormous relief across the community, bringing a frightening evening to the best possible conclusion.

Tonight demonstrated Newhey and the wider Rochdale borough at its very best. Residents did not simply share a post and hope for good news. They put on their shoes, went outside and actively helped search for someone who needed them.

Credit must also go to Greater Manchester Police and everyone who supported the search, but special recognition is due to the countless members of the public who gave their time and refused to give up.

The borough should be very proud tonight. This was community spirit in its purest form, and the outcome is the great news everyone had been hoping for.

Out of respect for Christine and her family, no further personal or medical details should be shared unless released through official channels.
